text: A room can feel stuffy even when the temperature is comfortable because “comfort” depends on more than heat. High humidity makes the air feel heavy and can slow the evaporation of moisture from skin, so the space may feel clammy or stale. Low airflow also contributes: when air is not moving or being replaced, odors, moisture, and exhaled air can build up, creating a closed-in feeling. Even at a pleasant temperature, a room with poor ventilation may seem less fresh. Opening a window, using a fan, or improving air circulation can make the same temperature feel much more comfortable.
task: Explain why a room can feel stuffy even when the temperature is comfortable. Discuss humidity and airflow without giving medical advice.
